## Step 3 / List 2 — likely matches needing confirmation (26)

Surfaced by the `split-audit.mjs` detectors:

- **edit distance** — scaled to name length: 2 chars allowed at 8+ characters, 1 at 6–7, none below 6.
- **prefix** — one name is a strict prefix of the other with 1–3 extra words, tested both before and after legal-suffix stripping. The *stem shared by* count is how many other canonicals the same stem prefixes; a high count means the stem is a common word, not a split.

Three further rules are **extensions, not part of `split-audit.mjs`** — flagged in the Rule column so their findings can be weighted lower. The original two rules alone missed every example named in the brief:

- **token-wise** — same token count, every token either identical, an abbreviation of its counterpart, within a scaled edit distance, or sharing a 4+ character root. `Vancouver Isl Brewery` → `Vancouver Island Brewing` is 5 edits apart and is not a strict prefix, so neither original rule reaches it.
- **containment** — the shorter name sits intact inside the longer one but not at the start, so the prefix rule cannot see it (`House of A La Ligne` inside `ALL Movement (House of A La Ligne)`).
- **shared stem** — both names open with the same token(s) and then diverge. Fires only when that stem prefixes **3 or fewer** other canonicals, so common openers cannot trigger it.

Write `match`, `new`, or `?` in the Decision column.

## Step 5 — nested folders (1)

Folders that contain sub-folders rather than only files. Everything else in the set holds its reports directly.

| Folder | Depth | Files direct | Files total | Inner shape |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Admin Slayer - Spring Planning | 4 | 0 | 4 | `2019 - 2020` [year] → `Admin Slayer` [name, 1 file] + `Spring Planning` [name, 1 file]<br>`2020 - 2021` [year] → 2 files direct |

**Shape:** `<client-pair>/<year>/<client>/report`. The top folder names *two* clients (`Admin Slayer`, `Spring Planning`) who were reviewed together. Under `2019 - 2020` each client got its own sub-folder and its own report; under `2020 - 2021` the pair shares one combined report filed directly, with no client sub-folder. So the year level is consistent but the client level is not — it exists in one year and not the other.

**Consequence for a later mapping task:** this one folder carries reports for two different clients. It cannot map to a single canonical. `Admin Slayer` matches an existing canonical (49 files); `Spring Planning` matches another (12 files). Both appear as candidates in List 2 above.

⚠️ **A shadow copy exists outside the client set.** The excluded `Strategy Meeting Reports/` folder contains its own `Admin Slayer - Spring Planning/` with `Admin Slayer/` and `Spring Planning/` sub-folders holding 4 more files (`.pdf` + `.pptx` of the same two reports). That folder was excluded at Step 1 as non-client, so those files are outside every count in this document. Worth a look before any copy or mapping step — the same reports appear in two places.

## Notes

- Detection is string-based only. No file contents were read, no model was asked to judge. Every row in List 2 is a candidate for review, not a finding.
- List 1 is reported as confident but was **not** applied — no canonical was created, renamed, or merged.
- Two of the five rules (`edit distance`, `prefix`) come from `scripts/split-audit.mjs`; three (`token-wise`, `containment`, `shared stem`) are extensions added here. The Rule column says which, so extension findings can be weighted lower.
- Nothing under `OPERATIONS/Contracts` was touched.
- The known `src/tools/dropbox.js:99-101` issue was left alone.
